text.p: Norwest Corp said Thrusday its non-performing assets totaled $200.0 million at December 31, down $31.0 million from September 30, 1996, and $6.0 million below the year-ago level.
As a percent of loans, leases and other real estate owned, non-performing assets were 0.51 percent as of December 31, compared with 0.58 percent as of September 30 and 0.57 percent a year ago.
Earlier, Norwest reported fourth quarter earnings of $0.81 a share, up from $0.72 a year ago. For 1996, Norwest earned $3.07 a share after a $0.03 charge, compared with $2.76 a primary share in 1995.
Norwest said 1996 was its 22nd consecutive year of record earnings.

"This latest record year was achieved despite a very challenging period for the consumer finance industry with rising delinquencies and charge-offs," David Wood, chairman of the Norwest Financial Inc unit, said in a statement.
He added Norwest had one-time, after-tax charges of $9.5 million in 1996 to write off its remaining original acquisition goodwill and settlement of litigation.
